name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. Domain=npc_turn_phase; descriptor 'team1' is a meaningful battle team ID (team 1 = NPC allies; team 2 = player, team 0 = enemy per fd2_enemy_turn_phase_team0 / TEAM_ENEMY), NOT an address residue. Name accurately reflects the per-frame AI loop over bTeam==1 chars. Caller fd2_run_full_turn_cycle uses it as 'Phase C - NPC turn'.
purpose: Per-frame AI turn loop over team-1 (NPC ally) characters: dispatch each eligible char's action, run its post-action consequence handler and the per-chapter scripted-event handler, breaking on a chapter/battle-end event.
logic_summary: Clears battle_anim_phase, then loops i in [0, party_member_count). Each iteration: reset anim_phase=0, flush keyboard buffer, set ai_post_action_consequence_idx=0xFF. If char[i] is bTeam==1 AND (bFlags & 0x81)==0 (not dead/not acted) AND sleep flag==0, call fd2_enemy_turn_action_dispatcher(i,1). Then, if consequence idx != 0xFF, invoke ai_post_action_consequence_table[idx]; always invoke chapter_post_action_handler_table[current_chapter_id]; break if chapter_event_or_battle_end_code != 0.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effects only: advances NPC-ally AI for one turn phase, mutating runtime char state and battle/chapter globals via dispatched handlers.

comment_original_issue: src comment was correct but terse: omitted the team-1 = NPC-ally / Phase-C context, the per-iteration skip conditions (dead/acted/asleep), the per-iteration anim_phase reset + keyboard flush, and the event-flag break.
notes: Decompilation, src, and caller (fd2_run_full_turn_cycle Phase C) are mutually consistent. Field offsets: bFlags +5, bTeam +6, sleep flag +0x26, RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE 0x50 (matches fd2-knowledge 80-byte runtime char). Minor readability nit (not a logic bug, out of scope for comment/name stage): this function uses literal 1 for the team check while sibling fd2_enemy_turn_phase_team0 uses named TEAM_ENEMY; a TEAM_NPC_ALLY constant could be introduced later but that is a code change beyond name/comment scope so not done here. Note: the function-pointer table calls pass (i) in src vs () in Ghidra decomp -- this is pre-existing verified game logic, not touched.
